title: Alexander in Egypt
objective: After this level you can explain how Alexander the Great took Egypt.
summary: In 332 BCE Egypt welcomed Alexander the Great and the Persian satrap surrendered. Alexander was crowned at Memphis, hailed as son of Amun at Siwa, founded Alexandria and was buried there.

cards.headline: In 332 BCE, Egypt welcomed a foreign conqueror as its deliverer.
cards.body: Alexander the Great took Egypt without a real fight. Then he set about becoming a proper pharaoh.

cards.headline: No battle needed
cards.body: Egypt was still under Persian rule when Alexander, king of Macedonia, arrived in November 332 BCE. The Persian governor, the satrap Mazaces, surrendered, and the people welcomed Alexander as their deliverer. Picture tenants throwing a party for the new landlord. After Persia, the bar was low.

cards.headline: Playing pharaoh
cards.body: At Memphis, Alexander sacrificed to the sacred Apis bull and was crowned with the double crown of the pharaohs. Remember it from Level 6? White and red together: Upper and Lower Egypt under one king. Then he went to the oracle of Amun in the Siwa oasis, where the priest greeted him as “son of Amun,” the traditional greeting for a pharaoh. A Macedonian, hailed in the pharaohs’ own words.
cards.callout: Crowned at Memphis, greeted as son of Amun at Siwa

cards.headline: A city, and a body
cards.body: Alexander founded a new city near the Nile’s western arm, between the sea and Lake Mareotis, sheltered by the island of Pharos: Alexandria. He didn’t stay to see it grow. He died in Babylon in 323 BCE, and his general Ptolemy diverted his body to Egypt. It ended up in a golden coffin in Alexandria. Alive, Alexander left Egypt behind. Dead, he came back to stay.

cards.headline: Alexander in Egypt: met
learned: Egypt welcomed Alexander in 332 BCE; Persia’s satrap surrendered
He was crowned with the double crown at Memphis
At Siwa he was greeted as son of Amun
He founded Alexandria and was buried there

questions.prompt: How did the Persian satrap of Egypt respond when Alexander arrived in 332 BCE?

options.label: He held Memphis through a long siege
options.rationale: There was no siege; he gave up.

options.label: He fled south to the kingdom of Kush
He had himself crowned as pharaoh

questions.explanation: The satrap Mazaces surrendered, and Egyptians welcomed Alexander as their deliverer.

questions.prompt: Why did it matter that the priest at Siwa greeted Alexander as “son of Amun”?

options.label: It made Alexander the high priest of Amun
options.rationale: It was a royal greeting, not a priesthood.

options.label: It ordered Alexander to leave Egypt
options.rationale: It welcomed him as a king.

options.label: It was an insult reserved for foreigners
It was the traditional greeting for a pharaoh

questions.explanation: Being called son of Amun was how a pharaoh was traditionally greeted, so it treated Alexander as Egypt’s king.

questions.prompt: Alexander was crowned at Memphis with the double crown. From Level 6, what did that crown stand for?

options.label: Egypt and Persia joined under one king
options.rationale: It stood for Egypt’s own two lands.

options.label: The king’s role as high priest of Amun
Upper and Lower Egypt united under one king
Victory over the Sea Peoples
options.rationale: It was far older than that war.

questions.explanation: The double crown combined the white crown of Upper Egypt and the red crown of Lower Egypt.
